correctness.rationale: The classification is mathematically correct. Independently, writing z=−it gives the real cubic f=t³−γt²+(a²+b²)t−γb². Its discriminant is the negative of the record's quadratic in γ², and the quadratic discriminant is a²(a²−8b²)³. At a²>8b² the two γ² roots are positive by their sum and product; discriminant signs give three real t's between them, with coalescence at the endpoints, and one outside. Matching coefficients of (t−t_0)³ forces t_0=√3 b and a²=8b², so the off-cusp repeated eigenvalues have multiplicity two, not three. The phrase 'double discriminant root' in the proof should mean a double eigenvalue, not a double zero of the discriminant in γ². The first two row equations determine the eigenvector from its nonzero first coordinate, giving nullity one and Im z=−γ|v_1|²/||v||²<0. For K_m,n, order the active basis as lossy site, opposite-class mean, same-class remaining mean. The trimer then has a=√n, b=√[n(m−1)] and nonzero determinant iγb²; the orthogonal complement is annihilated because its sums within both unmarked cells vanish. The m=1 block is a dimer whose repeated nonzero eigenvalue at γ=2√n has nullity one. Both sites qualify in K_1,1. The proof is sufficient without finite tests; the checker mentioned in RESULT.md is not present among the furnished evidence paths, and its author-reported run is not an independent reproduction.

evidence: Putting y=x², the prior repeated-root curve has (a/b)²=(y+1)²/(y−1) for y>1, minimizing at y=3 with value 8; two y's occur above 8, one at 8. Eliminating y using γ/b=2y^(3/2)/(y−1) gives the same two squared strengths. The prior curve is the boundary of spectral regions for the identical real cubic; its discriminant changes sign at each off-cusp point, so all three roots are imaginary in the bounded interval. No new spectral equation is needed.

For the graph, the three marked cells are equitable, with edges between the one-site cell and opposite class, and between the two unmarked cells, but no other active entries. This gives the orthonormal quotient entries directly by cell sizes. Applying the prior phase diagram to the resulting ratio and the prior dimer line exhausts the graph cases.

evidence: In arXiv:2601.09628v2 take N=2 lossless guides of coupling κ and one dissipative auxiliary guide of coupling α and onsite −iγ_paper/2. Reverse sites and set κ=b, α=a, γ_paper=2γ. The determinant (s+γ_paper/2)θ_2+α²θ_1 has θ_2=s²+κ² and θ_1=s (with dimensions restored); at s=−it/i=−t this yields exactly the frozen real cubic up to sign.
Equivalently write x=t/b. Eq. (10) reduces to (a/b)²=(x²+1)²/(x²−1), γ/b=2x³/(x²−1), for x>1. The equal-coupling model of Joglekar–Harter in Eq. (7) gives only the narrower no-EP branch.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The determinant and signed damping parameter match as functions, not merely at one sample threshold. The auxiliary-guide formulation is precisely a loss-only endpoint trimer under the indicated convention.

originality.rationale: The 4 October 2026 version of arXiv:2601.09628 already treats the very same passive, unequal-coupling trimer in its auxiliary-guide section (not its uniform-chain section). Its analytic repeated-root boundary Eq. (10), Fig. 6 N=2 panel and Table I N=2 row cover the cusp, order and adjacent spectral sectors after reversing sites and converting loss conventions. The exact radical expressions merely eliminate the parameter in that boundary. Its N=1 model also gives the dimer threshold. The graph statement follows mechanically from the standard constant-on-cells quotient and the known N=2 and N=1 results; lack of an explicit K_m,n label in that paper does not restore originality.
residual_risks: The inaccessible Yalouz–Pouthier article could show more direct star coverage; that access limitation does not drive this fail.

value.rationale: An exact loss-only cusp and full classification would be a useful boundary if not already determined, but here the main diagram is a known auxiliary-guide specialization. The extra radical form requires only elimination, and the unweighted complete-bipartite corollary is just the canonical twin-cell quotient into two already solved cases plus annihilated dark modes. No independent new invariant or obstruction survives that justifies a repaired finding.
